transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Xu (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (CTO Saturn Payments), Priya Singh (Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Infra)

Summary: Initial dedicated capacity discovery focused on reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst strategy and scaling expectations. Customer has strict data residency and compliance requirements and is evaluating Dedicated vs Private deployment for production. Agreed next steps include pricing, benchmark pilot, and architecture deep dive for VPC/KMS.

Topics: Dedicated capacity sizing, isolation and tenancy, burst capacity, autoscaling policies, encryption and KMS, SOC 2 / auditability, VPC peering and network egress, latency vs cost tradeoffs, benchmarking plan.

Action items (captured): see metadata section

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, im Jordan from Redwood, im the AE on this account, appreciate you taking the time. quick intro round?
[00:12] Alex: yeah this is Alex moreno, CTO at Saturn Payments, Priya and Carlos are on as well. we run payment risk models and a chat assist system for merchants, looking at moving some inference workloads off public endpoints.
[00:24] Priya S: hey all, priya singh, head of ML. main things for us are latency, isolation and cost predictability. we have strict pci style controls and need to know where data sits.
[00:35] Carlos: carlos ruiz, infra lead. we manage our cloud infra on gcp, bigmix of k8s clusters and some on prem for regulatory cases.
[00:44] Jordan: great, thanks. agenda: understand current stack and constraints, workloads and qps, then talk dedicated capacity options, burst strategy, security controls and next steps. sound good?
[00:53] Alex: yep good.

[01:05] Priya R (Redwood SE): quick clarifying question, when you say latency requirements what are you aiming for p50 and p95? and do you have token lengths, sequence lengths?
[01:14] Priya S: for our chat assist p50 target is sub 200ms for short prompts, p95 under 800ms. typical sequences 60 100 tokens, sometimes longer for reranks. batch jobs for risk scoring run offline but we want dedicated for online inference.
[01:28] Jordan: got it, so two patterns real time chat and occasional long seq scoring jobs. whats qps during peak?
[01:36] Alex: peak QPS around 120 reqs per second across our stack, chat is the majority. risk scoring spikes can push longer jobs but lower qps.

[01:50] Sam Xu (Redwood SE): two quick architecture notes: dedicated capacity = reserved GPU pools with isolation, we can provision burst pools for transient peaks. our runtime supports continuous batching and kv cache to reduce per token cost but that interacts with isolation and multi tenancy.
[02:05] Carlos: do you support private deployment? we looked at Redwood Private but want to understand tradeoffs vs Dedicated hosted dedicated.
[02:12] Jordan: yeah good question. Dedicated is our reserved hosted capacity per customer with tenant isolation at runtime and data segregation. Private is full VPC or on prem where control plane is customer managed. dedicated gives fastest time to value and managed infra, private is for stricter regulatory requirements.
[02:30] Priya S: for us data residency and audit logs are must haves. we need key management integrations and proof of SOC 2 and possibly ISO.

[02:44] Jordan: we have SOC 2 and ISO docs we can share, and we support KMS integrations for customer-managed keys, and audit logging at the route and token level. ill send the package.

[03:00] Alex: great. curious on GPUs - what hardware do you offer for Dedicated and how do you recommend sizing?
[03:08] Priya R: our standard Dedicated configs run on A100 or H100 variants depending on region. sizing depends on model footprint and latency targets. for your QPS and p95 target we usually recommend starting with a 4x A100 pool and then instrumenting with our workload profiler, but we can prototype.
[03:26] Carlos: any support for mixed instance pools or auto-scaling? we have bursty traffic and sometimes procurement delays.
[03:33] Sam: yes we support mixed pools and configurable autoscaling policies. burst capacity can be either pre-warmed reserved burst nodes or on-demand spillover to a compatible hosted tier. note that spillover to public hosted endpoints has different data controls so if you need strict isolation you can use dedicated burst capacity only.
[03:52] Priya S: so if we need isolation even during bursts we need to commit to burst nodes reserved?
[03:58] Priya R: right, either reserved burst capacity or private deployment for full isolation. also there's model variant fallback, if exact model not available we can route to a quantized or smaller variant to preserve availability while staying within isolation policy.

[04:18] Alex: pricing question then, how do you charge for burst reserved vs on demand?
[04:24] Jordan: we charge base reserved monthly commit for Dedicated nodes, and burst reserved is a higher committed tier you can enable. on demand spillover is usage billed but may not meet same SLA. ill include pricing tiers in the follow up.

[04:40] Carlos: network since we run on GCP whats peering model, egress, and ip allowlisting?
[04:46] Sam: we support VPC peering and private endpoints. egress charges depend on region, but we can restrict routes and provide IP allowlist. we also support SAML SSO and RBAC for admin access.

[05:02] Priya S: KMS details - do you support customer-managed keys and HSMs? we have requirements to rotate keys and have auditable key usage.
[05:10] Priya R: yes we support KMS integrations and can log KMS operations in audit. if you need HSM-backed service or on prem HSM we can discuss Private deployment options.

[05:24] Alex: what's the typical onboarding timeline for Dedicated?
[05:28] Jordan: we do a two phase onboarding - pilot + production roll. pilot can be as fast as 2 weeks if you provide access and contract, typical end-to-end to production around 4 to 8 weeks depending on network and security review.

[05:44] Carlos: what about model updates and version pinning? we need reproducible model versions for audits.
[05:49] Sam: you can pin model versions and we provide rollouts, canary deploys, and automatic fallback. we also store model audit metadata and serve from immutable artifact ids.

[06:05] Priya S: benchmarks. we want to run a benchmark with our prompts and see latency and cost. what do you need from us?
[06:12] Priya R: ideally we get sample prompt sets, typical sequence lengths, and an estimate of concurrency. we will run a 3 day benchmark on a mirror of production traffic on a 4x A100 pool and return token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
[06:27] Alex: ok we can share prompt sets and a small dataset, will that require any NDA?
[06:31] Jordan: we have an existing NDA template, but for basic benchmarks we can do an anonymized run. for data with PHI or sensitive info we can use Private deployment or redaction.

[06:48] Sam: quick note on KV cache and batching - these reduce token spend but caching is per-tenant and needs warmup. in high tail latency scenarios batching improves throughput but may add latency for single request flows.
[07:02] Priya S: hmmm that aligns with our concerns. most of our chat is single-turn and we cant add 100ms if that breaks UX.
[07:11] Priya R: understood. we can tune batch windows and prefer continuous batching with small latency SLOs to hit your p50 target.

[07:24] Jordan: any concerns on compliance from legal or procurement that we should be aware of early?
[07:29] Alex: procurement will ask about data retention policies, legal wants encryption at rest and in transit and audit capabilities. we may need background checks for privileged access in some cases.
[07:39] Jordan: we can share our retention and encryption docs; we support route-level audit logs and can provide access reports.

[07:50] Carlos: bring up an edge case, some of our risk scoring runs on prem for latency reasons. is hybrid ok?
[07:57] Sam: yes hybrid is supported. Dedicated handles hosted reserved nodes and we can combine with on prem for ultra low latency. Private gives full on prem options.

[08:10] Alex: ok timeline, procurement wants a Q2 pilot and decision by early Q3. is that feasible?
[08:16] Jordan: absolutely. pilot in Q2 is reasonable. we'll propose pilot plan and SOW.

[08:25] Priya R: two technical clarifications - do you use beam search or sampling in production for chat, and any specialized models?
[08:33] Priya S: we use top-p sampling for chat and a smaller distilled model for quick responses, larger models for risk scoring.

[08:41] Sam: on the runtime side we support attention kernel selection and quantization profiles. for your distill model we may recommend int8 quantization to reduce costs.

[08:53] Alex: what's the maintenance window for Dedicated, any planned downtime?
[08:58] Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime. we aim for minimal maintenance windows, rolling updates are standard and we match maintenance windows with customers where possible.

[09:10] Priya S: security reviews - do you provide penetration test reports and SOC2 Type II?
[09:15] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test summaries available under NDA. will share in follow up.

[09:25] Alex: can you expose per-route tracing? we need token-level cost attribution.
[09:29] Sam: yes we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model.

[09:36] Priya R: ok just to make sure i understand your scaling expectation - you said 120 qps peak, p95 under 800ms, some longer sequences - we recommend 4x A100 as a starting point with a reserved burst pool of 1x A100 for spikes, and run a bench to validate. does that sound right?
[09:53] Alex: yes sounds like a good starting point.

[10:02] Jordan: any blockers for pilot?
[10:06] Priya S: procurement needs pricing and security docs, ml needs benchmark harness and AR/QA, infra needs VPC peering details.
[10:14] Jordan: will do. we'll send pricing, SOC2 and ISO docs, and benchmark config.

[10:20] Sam: one more note on model variant fallback - if you need strict isolation we will only allow fallback to models in your dedicated pool or to pre-approved quantized variants.

[10:33] Carlos: ok cool. question about billing granularity - per token, instance hour?
[10:38] Jordan: for Dedicated reserved we invoice a monthly capacity fee per GPU hour in the pool plus a small per-token usage for extra features; for on demand spillover it's per token / per-hour usage. exact numbers in the pricing doc.

[10:55] Priya S: regarding compliance, we need support for VPC flow logs and audit exports to our SIEM, can you stream logs?
[11:03] Sam: yes, we can stream audit logs to your cloud logging or to a S3/GCS bucket with controlled access.

[11:12] Alex: ok are there any known performance regressions with quantized models for scoring? we cant reduce accuracy too much.
[11:19] Priya R: quantization can introduce small delta in output; we do quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can run A/B tests during pilot to validate.

[11:31] Jordan: anything else we should cover?
[11:34] Priya S: just want to ensure SLA on latency - can you commit to p95 targets in SLA?
[11:40] Jordan: we can discuss latency SLAs in the enterprise contract. often SLAs are a function of the committed hardware profile and network. we'll include sample SLA language.

[11:52] Alex: ok great. recap next steps?
[11:56] Jordan: i'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO and pen test summaries, priya will share benchmark harness and config, we'll schedule infra deep dive for VPC peering next week. customer confirm pilot scope and GPU type.

[12:11] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[12:14] Jordan: thanks all.

Note: timestamps are approximate and transcription shows occasional mis-hearings e g K-V cash for KV cache, and product name sometimes as Redwood runtime or Redwood rent time. There is occasional speaker overlap and filler words.
